# Content-read call-site inventory (WF-303 / SUB-2)

**Charter:** [WF-301 — C011 The wf-resolver MCP serves bundled-doc content, killing raw reads of plugin files](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-301).
**This issue:** [WF-303 — SUB-2 Establish the reviewed content-read call-site inventory](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-303).
**Kind:** change-control / inventory artifact — **no runtime code.** Not read at skill runtime (so the CLAUDE.md §7 ops/reference budget does not apply, exactly as for its C008 sibling).
**Generated by:** claude-opus-4-8

This is the single reviewable inventory of every **runtime content-read call site** across
the wf core plugin and every pack — every place a skill or agent, at runtime, performs a
raw `Read`/`Glob` of a **bundled non-skill document body**: a capability **fragment**, a
`_contracts/*.ops.md` **contract-ops** doc, a `_shared/*` **shared** doc, a skill
`references/*` **template**, or a pack's **`profile.template.json`**. It assigns **every**
such call site exactly one of the **five content classes then in scope** and its owning sweep slice, so
the C011 consumer sweep is bounded against a reviewed list and cannot silently expand.

> **This is a NEW inventory, distinct from C008's.** The predecessor
> [`docs/resolver-consumer-inventory.md`](resolver-consumer-inventory.md) (WF-273 / SUB-12)
> catalogued **discovery** consumers — config, registry, provider, path, and plugin-root
> *resolution*. It **deliberately excluded document bodies**: its §2 counts `_contracts/*`,
> `references/*`, `manifest.md`, and `profile.template.json` as resolver **inputs/targets,
> not consumers.** C011 serves those bodies, so — per C008's own change-control rule — a
> **new** reviewed inventory is required for the new class. This is that inventory. Where
> C008 read a *path/metadata* through the resolver, C011 reads the *body*; the two are
> orthogonal and this document covers only the latter.

> **Current resolver call contract.** Before every resolver MCP invocation named in this historical
> inventory, run `pwd -P` and pass the returned absolute current Agent/session workspace directory
> explicitly as schema-required `workspaceRoot`. In a linked-worktree Agent, that cwd is the Agent's
> own worktree; never inherit the parent session's root. Omission is a hard schema error; there is no
> default or fallback.
> Metadata queries remain body-free; the distinct `resolve_content` tool serves approved bodies.
> It now accepts six classes: the five inventoried here plus `slot`, which composes a per-skill
> composition point from `skill` + `point`.
>
> **Change control.** This inventory is the reviewed baseline that bounds the SUB-3…SUB-7
> sweep. A newly discovered content-read call site — or a new skill/agent/pack/doc surface
> added later — requires an **explicit reviewed update here and a class/owner assignment**,
> not silent scope expansion into an existing sweep slice. The class set is **exactly the
> five** named below (C011 Scope IN); nothing else is in scope.

## 1. The five content classes

Every entry below carries exactly one class and its owning slice:

| # | Content class | The bundled body read | Owning sweep slice |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **fragment** | a capability **fragment** body (`capabilities/*/fragments/*.md` — provider `delivery.ops.md`/`tracker.ops.md`, the `finding`/`guidance`/`pre-commit` fragments, `finding-contract.md`, `retrospective.md`) | **SUB-3 → [WF-304](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-304)** |
| 2 | **shared** | a `_shared/*` convention doc (`plugins/wf/skills/_shared/pipeline-conventions.md`) | **SUB-4 → [WF-305](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-305)** |
| 3 | **contract-ops** | a `_contracts/*.ops.md` runtime-ops contract | **SUB-5 → [WF-306](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-306)** |
| 4 | **references** | a skill `references/*` template read on a skill's own write/execution path | **SUB-6 → [WF-307](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-307)** |
| 5 | **profile** | a pack's `profile.template.json` body (read by init to seed on divergence) | **SUB-7 → [WF-308](https://linear.app/neurasphere/issue/WF-308)** |

Ordering note: SUB-3 and SUB-4 have **no dependency edge** but both create/append the OUT-2
CI grep script — per the charter's accepted warning F4.1 a runner must serialize SUB-3
before SUB-4, never dispatch them in parallel. (F4.2: the grep gates OUT-2, not OUT-1.)

## 2. Method, coverage, and the acceptance cross-check

**Scanned exhaustively** (indexed grep + full read of each surface): every core skill
(`plugins/wf/skills/*`), every core agent (`plugins/wf/agents/*`), and every skill, agent,
and capability fragment across all eight packs — wf-git, wf-ado, wf-linear, wf-node-ts,
wf-audit, wf-browser-qa, wf-angular, wf-review.

**What counts as a content-read call site.** A location in a skill/agent (or a fragment that
in turn reads another fragment) that, at runtime, performs — or instructs — a raw
`Read`/`Glob` of one of the five bundled non-skill body classes. Crucially:

- A **resolver-metadata** call (`resolve_config`, `resolve_registry`, `resolve_provider`,
  `resolve_profile`, `resolve_plugin_root`, `inspect_pack`, `register_pack`) is **not** a
  content read — these metadata tools return paths/metadata/values, never a body. Body serving
  belongs exclusively to `resolve_content`.
- The C008 body-free split is why so many reads survive: `resolve_provider` returns the
  `fragmentPath`, then the consumer **still raw-reads that fragment body in its own
  context** (`invocation-runtime.ops.md` step 4 / run-scoped forwarding "carries no
  fragment body"). That surviving raw read is the fragment-class call site C011 targets.

**Dispatch shape drives who reads a fragment** (confirmed against every `capabilities/*/manifest.md`):

- `inline: <rel-path>` fragments are read **in-context by the firing boot** — `git`
  `delivery.ops.md`, `ado`/`linear` `tracker.ops.md`, `node-ts` `test-authoring.md`,
  `sr` `self-review.md`.
- `subagent: <agent>` fragments are read **by the dispatched agent's own boot** — the five
  `audit` lens fragments (via the auditor agents) and the `qa-execution` providers (via the
  `qa-engine`/`qa-host` subagents, which read their own skill+references, not a fragment
  file). `retrospective.md` is not a phase fragment; the `audit-retrospective` agent
  self-reads it.

**Acceptance cross-check** (§7) greps `plugins/**` for the five content-read shapes and
demonstrates that every hit maps to an entry here or to a named exclusion — nothing in the
five classes is absent.

## 3. Target-document universe

The bundled non-skill bodies the sweep serves through the resolver, by class:

| Class | Body files |
|---|---|
| **fragment** | `wf-git/capabilities/git/fragments/delivery.ops.md`; `wf-ado/capabilities/ado/fragments/tracker.ops.md`; `wf-linear/capabilities/linear/fragments/tracker.ops.md`; `wf-node-ts/capabilities/node-ts/fragments/test-authoring.md`; `wf-audit/capabilities/sr/fragments/self-review.md`; `wf-audit/capabilities/audit/fragments/{correctness,security,convention,consistency,operational}.md`; `wf-audit/capabilities/audit/fragments/finding-contract.md`; `wf-audit/capabilities/audit/fragments/retrospective.md` |
| **shared** | `plugins/wf/skills/_shared/pipeline-conventions.md` |
| **contract-ops** | `plugins/wf/skills/_contracts/capability-registry.ops.md`; `.../invocation-runtime.ops.md`; `.../pack-onboarding.ops.md` |
| **references** | the skill `references/*` templates enumerated in §4.4 (18 across core + wf-angular + wf-browser-qa) |
| **profile** | `wf-angular/capabilities/angular/profile.template.json`; `wf-audit/capabilities/audit/profile.template.json` |

> The `.md` **reference halves** of the provider fragments (`git/.../delivery.md`,
> `ado`/`linear` `tracker.md`) and every `capabilities/*/references/onboarding.md` and
> `_contracts/*.contract.md` are the **reference (non-runtime) halves** of the ops/reference

## 4. Call-site inventory

### 4.1 Fragment class → SUB-3 (WF-304)

The largest class. Split into three read patterns.

**(a) Provider-fragment reads — `delivery.ops.md` (delivery surface).** After
`resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot: "<Agent/session absolute current workspace directory>", surface: "delivery" })` returns the record, the boot raw-reads the resolved
`delivery.ops.md` body to dispatch the operation. Every delivery-operation boot is a call
site:

| Consumer | Notes |
|---|---|
| `wf/skills/spec` | + tracker (see (a′)) |
| `wf/skills/plan` | `current-branch-query` |
| `wf/skills/tasks` | |
| `wf/skills/implement` | + forwards the resolution record |
| `wf/skills/run` | 3 delivery ops off one resolution |
| `wf/skills/verify-spec` | |
| `wf/skills/verify-fix` | |
| `wf/skills/constitution` | `workspace-root-resolve` |
| `wf/skills/qa-gen` | |
| `wf/skills/qa-run` | |
| `wf/skills/qa-auto` | |
| `wf/skills/qa-followup` | |
| `wf/skills/tt` | |
| `wf/skills/tf` | + tracker |
| `wf/skills/classify` | delivery only on branch-inference |
| `wf/skills/triage` | + tracker |
| `wf/skills/lite` | + tracker |
| `wf/skills/index` | delivery only in id-inferred path |
| `wf/skills/standup` | + tracker |
| `wf/skills/pr` | single resolution point (delivery + tracker) |
| `wf/agents/branch` | + lazy tracker |
| `wf/agents/commit` | |
| `wf/agents/pr` | + tracker |
| `wf/agents/context-distiller` | optional CI-log read op only |
| `wf-audit/agents/audit-retrospective` | 3 delivery read ops |
| `wf-audit/capabilities/audit/fragments/retrospective.md` | fragment-internal: reads delivery ops (nested fragment→fragment read) |
| `wf-review/skills/review-pr` | |
| `wf-review/skills/address-pr` | |
| `wf-browser-qa/skills/qa-engine` | optional on branch-inference |
| `wf-angular/skills/qa-host` | |
| `wf-angular/skills/test-page` | |

> The `wf/skills/branch` and `wf/skills/commit` skills are thin `[Task]` wrappers — the
> **agent** boot performs the fragment read; the skill delegates. `wf/agents/phase-runner`
> re-pays the wrapped phase's delivery read per iteration (transitive; not a separate
> target).

**(a′) Provider-fragment reads — `tracker.ops.md` (tracker surface: `ado` **or** `linear`,
whichever is registered; partitioned single-owner).** Consumers reading the resolved
tracker fragment body: `wf/skills/spec`, `wf/skills/triage`, `wf/skills/lite`,
`wf/skills/standup`, `wf/skills/tf`, `wf/skills/pr`, `wf/agents/pr`, `wf/agents/branch`
(lazy no-artifact path).

**(b) Phase-/pre-commit-fragment reads — `inline` dispatch bodies.**

| Consumer | Fragment read | Phase/kind |
|---|---|---|
| `wf/skills/implement` | `node-ts/.../test-authoring.md` | implement · guidance (inline; when node-ts registered) |
| `wf/skills/tt` | `node-ts/.../test-authoring.md` | implement · guidance (aggregated) |
| `wf/agents/commit` | `sr/.../self-review.md` | pre-commit · finding (inline seam) |
| `wf/agents/commit` | `audit/.../correctness.md` | reused intra-plugin by `self-review.md` (nested fragment→fragment read) |

> `verify-spec` fires `verify`/`finding`, `qa-gen` fires `qa-generation`/`scenario`,
> `qa-auto`/`qa-followup` walk `qa-execution` — all currently resolve to **`subagent:`**
> providers or to **no active fragment** (migration `scenario`/`task-list` unshipped), so
> the firing skill reads **no** inline body; the dispatched agent does (pattern (c)).
> `constitution`/`tasks` sweep `article`/`task-list` rows that live in `manifest.md`
> **metadata** (served by `resolve_registry`), not in fragment bodies — not a fragment
> read.

**(c) Subagent self-boot fragment reads — the dispatched agent reads its own bundled fragment(s).**

| Consumer (agent) | Fragment(s) read |
|---|---|
| `wf-audit/agents/correctness-auditor` | `finding-contract.md` + `correctness.md` |
| `wf-audit/agents/security-auditor` | `finding-contract.md` + `security.md` |
| `wf-audit/agents/convention-auditor` | `finding-contract.md` + `convention.md` |
| `wf-audit/agents/consistency-auditor` | `finding-contract.md` + `consistency.md` |
| `wf-audit/agents/operational-auditor` | `finding-contract.md` + `operational.md` |
| `wf-audit/agents/audit-retrospective` | `retrospective.md` |

> These self-boot reads are `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/capabilities/audit/fragments/…` raw reads
> of **fragment bodies** — in scope for C011. (C008 counted them as own-plugin *discovery*
> inputs and excluded them from the *resolver* inventory; for the *content* sweep they are
> genuine fragment-body reads and are listed here. The two framings are consistent — a
> fragment body is a resolver input **and** a content-read target.)

### 4.3 Contract-ops class → SUB-5 (WF-306)

Runtime reads of a `_contracts/*.ops.md` body (to follow a procedure or emit diagnosis text
the doc defines). Listed inclusively for change-control; the sweep adjudicates per site
whether C008's typed MCP (`resolve_gate`/`resolve_provider`) already serves the cited text
or the raw read must be routed through the resolver content surface.

**`capability-registry.ops.md`** — read for the self-heal algorithm, surface operation
sets, and resolver-failure/diagnosis semantics:
`wf/skills/{spec, implement, verify-spec, verify-fix, qa-gen, qa-run, qa-auto, qa-followup,
tt, tf, triage, lite, pr, index, classify, standup}`; `wf/agents/{pr, commit, branch}`;
`wf-review/skills/{review-pr, address-pr}`; `wf-browser-qa/skills/qa-engine`;
`wf-angular/skills/{qa-host, test-page}`; `wf-audit/skills/init`;
`wf-browser-qa/skills/init`. Fragment-internal cites (nested reads): the provider fragments
`ado`/`linear` `tracker.ops.md`, `git` `delivery.ops.md`, and `audit`
`retrospective.md`/`sr` `self-review.md`.

**`invocation-runtime.ops.md`** — read for the phase-fire / direct-provider-resolution
procedure: `wf/skills/{spec, implement, tf, lite, pr, commit}`; `wf/agents/{pr, commit}`.

**`pack-onboarding.ops.md`** — **no live runtime consumer.** Only its `.contract.md` pair
and a non-runtime `wf-ado/.../references/onboarding.md` reference it; current init flows
route through the `inspect_pack`/`register_pack` MCP and do not read it. Recorded so the
class is provably covered (target present, zero surviving call sites).

### 4.5 Profile class → SUB-7 (WF-308)

Init reads the capability's `profile.template.json` **body** to seed a downstream override
`_local/profiles/<cap>.profile.json` **only on divergence** from the template default:

| Consumer | Template read |
|---|---|
| `wf-audit/skills/init` (Phase 3) | `wf-audit/capabilities/audit/profile.template.json` |
| `wf-angular/skills/init` | `wf-angular/capabilities/angular/profile.template.json` |

> `wf-angular/skills/qa-host` and `wf-angular/skills/test-page` do **not** read the template
> — they call `resolve_profile({ workspaceRoot: "<Agent/session absolute current workspace directory>", capability: "angular" })` for override-merged **values** (C008 R4) and
> state "this skill performs no direct profile-file read." Their `profile.template.json`
> mentions are precedence prose, not reads. Not call sites for this class.

## 5. Coverage ledger

| Class | Owner | Target docs | Call sites |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| fragment | SUB-3 / WF-304 | 11 | 32 delivery + 8 tracker + 4 inline phase/pre-commit + 6 subagent self-boot |
| shared | SUB-4 / WF-305 | 1 | 6 |
| contract-ops | SUB-5 / WF-306 | 3 | 20 (registry-ops) + 8 (invocation-runtime) + 0 (pack-onboarding) |
| references | SUB-6 / WF-307 | 18 templates | 14 consumers (18 template reads) |
| profile | SUB-7 / WF-308 | 2 | 2 |

Every content-read call site above has exactly one class and one named owning slice; there
is no catch-all. Counts are call sites (a consumer that reads two targets contributes to
each). The fragment class is dominated by the provider-fragment read, which recurs in
nearly every provider-operation boot — the single most widespread raw read C011 removes.

## 6. Explicit exclusions

Recorded as **inputs/targets or out-of-scope**, never as content-serving consumers:

| Excluded | Reason |
|---|---|
| **Skill bodies** (any read of a `skills/*/SKILL.md` body — e.g. init skills citing `plugins/wf/skills/resolve/SKILL.md`; the `phase-runner`/thin-wrapper reads of a wrapped SKILL) | Owned by the separate **Skill-tool charter**, not C011. C011 serves only the five *non-skill* bundled-doc classes. |
| **CI-only fixtures / validator inputs** (`_contracts/registry-fixtures/*`, `installed_plugins.fixture.json`, `validate-registry.sh`, the OUT-2 grep script, `plugins/wf/mcp/test/*`) | Read only by CI, never at skill runtime. Resolution/validation targets, not content-serving consumers. |
| **`manifest.md` reads** (init "resolve its manifest at `manifestPath`"; the `constitution`/`tasks` `article`/`task-list` sweeps) | **Metadata**, served by C008 `resolve_registry`/`inspect_pack` — not a fragment *body*. Not one of the five classes. |
| **`_contracts/*.contract.md` reference halves** (`capability-registry.contract.md` §profile-seeding cited by init; `invocation-runtime.contract.md`; `pack-onboarding.contract.md`; `invocation-mechanism.contract.md`) | The five classes name `_contracts/*.ops.md`, not `.contract.md`. The `.contract.md` files are reference (rationale) halves, out of the five classes by definition. |
| **`capabilities/*/references/onboarding.md`** (ado, angular, audit, sr, browser-qa, git, linear, node-ts, pr-review) | Reference (non-runtime) halves — the ops/reference split's rationale docs. Manifest prose "read by `init`" is **legacy**: current init flows use `inspect_pack`/`register_pack` and do not read them. Non-runtime → not a call site. |
| **Provider fragment `.md` reference halves** (`git/.../delivery.md`, `ado`/`linear` `tracker.md`) | The rationale halves paired with the `.ops.md` bodies; never read at boot (the `.ops.md` half is the runtime read, captured in §4.1). |
| **`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` own-`SKILL.md` self-boot** | The plugin runtime handing a component its own skill body — not a bundled non-skill doc read; and skill bodies are the separate charter regardless. (Own-*fragment* self-boot **is** in scope — §4.1(c).) |
| **Resolver-metadata calls** (`resolve_config`/`resolve_registry`/`resolve_provider`/`resolve_profile`/`resolve_plugin_root`/`inspect_pack`/`register_pack`) | Return paths/metadata/values, never a body (C008, delivered). Not raw reads; unchanged by C011. |

## 7. Acceptance cross-check

The reviewer runs these greps over `plugins/**`; every hit resolves to a §4 entry or a §6
exclusion, proving no content-read call site in the five classes is missing.

| # | Shape (grep pattern) | Class | Maps to |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_shared/` | shared | §4.2 (6 consumers) |
| 2 | `_contracts/.*\.ops\.md` / `capability-registry\.ops\.md` / `invocation-runtime` / `pack-onboarding` | contract-ops | §4.3 |
| 3 | `\]\(references/` and `references/…\.md` reads | references | §4.4 (18 templates); `capabilities/*/references/onboarding.md` → §6 exclusion |
| 4 | `profile\.template\.json` | profile | §4.5 (2 init reads); qa-host/test-page mentions → §4.5 note (values via `resolve_profile`) |
| 5 | `fragments/.*\.md` (inline dispatch) · `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/capabilities/.*/fragments/` (self-boot) · resolved `delivery.ops.md`/`tracker.ops.md` dispatch reads | fragment | §4.1(a)/(a′)/(b)/(c) |

**Residual-read guard (OUT-2).** After the SUB-3…SUB-7 sweep converts every §4 call site to
the resolver content surface, the OUT-2 acceptance grep (shape of
`plugins/wf/skills/_contracts/`'s CI grep script) must find **zero** raw-read instructions
for these five classes — no fallback carve-out. Any hit not reducible to a §6 exclusion is
a missed call site and fails CI. This inventory is the list that grep is checked against.

**Terminal-slice status (SUB-7 / WF-308).** All five per-class clauses are now consolidated
into the single composite gate `plugins/wf/skills/_contracts/content-read-out2-grep.sh`,
each scanning the whole marketplace (`plugins/**` — every plugin's `skills/` + `agents/`,
not just the core spine), wired into CI via `registry-fixtures/run.sh`. Zero hits across
all five classes = pass, with no raw-read carve-out. The last fragment-class residuals the
core-only SUB-3 sweep had left in the packs — the six wf-audit self-boot agents (the five
verify lenses + the composite retrospective), which raw-read their own
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/capabilities/audit/fragments/*.md` bodies — were converted to
`resolve_content` (`class: fragment`, `capability: audit`) in this slice (the five lens
agents drop their `tools:` allowlist so they inherit the always-loaded `wf-resolver` MCP,
per CLAUDE.md §8). The two profile-class init consumers (`wf-audit`, `wf-angular`) now
obtain their `profile.template.json` **body** at seed time through `resolve_content`
(`class: profile-template`). The other pack fragment consumers named as at-risk
(wf-review, wf-angular `qa-host`/`test-page`, wf-browser-qa `qa-engine`) were already
resolver-routed by the earlier slices — their remaining bundled-doc mentions are
bare-filename documentation pointers, not raw plugin-cache-path reads, and pass the gate
unchanged.

## 8. OUT-1 observation

**The unattended zero-prompt run (terminal slice — SUB-7 / WF-308).** OUT-1 asks that a
full `run --auto` pass on an **out-of-tree** (marketplace-consumed) install read every
bundled non-skill doc with **zero permission prompts for plugin-cache paths**. Unlike OUT-2
(a committed, CI-enforceable grep) OUT-1 is an **observed-behaviour** outcome; it is
recorded here as a reasoned observation grounded in the now-completed mechanism, honestly
noting what is and is not machine-checkable in this repo:

1. **Every content read now goes through one already-granted MCP surface.** The OUT-2
   composite grep proves **zero** raw `Read`/`Glob` instructions for any of the five
   content classes survive anywhere under `plugins/**`. Core and every pack obtain fragment,
   shared, contract-ops, references-template, and profile-template bodies exclusively via
   the bundled `wf-resolver` MCP's `resolve_content`, which reads the body with the
   **server's own Node `fs`** in its own process — never a caller-side file read of a
   version-pinned plugin-cache path.
2. **A `run --auto` pass touches bundled docs only through that surface.** The unattended
   runner and the phases/providers/subagents it drives (including the wf-audit verify
   lenses converted in this slice) reach every bundled doc through `resolve_content`, so
   the pass raises **no plugin-cache-path permission prompt** — the prompt class C011 set
   out to eliminate. The `wf-resolver` server is `alwaysLoad: true`, so its single tool-use
   grant is in force for the whole pass.
3. **The grant survives a version bump (OUT-3, reinforcing OUT-1).** The grant is keyed to
   the MCP tool, not to a version-pinned cache path, so a plugin version bump that relocates
   the cache does not re-prompt — no new per-path grant is needed (exercised hermetically by
   the recorded-root-first self-heal fixtures in `registry-fixtures/run.sh`).

**What is not directly executed here:** this repo is a marketplace source checkout, not a
live out-of-tree install with a running task, so a literal `run --auto` pass is not driven
in CI. The CI-enforceable proxy for OUT-1 is the **OUT-2 composite grep** (§7): because it
guarantees no raw-read *instruction* remains, the only path left for a content read is the
already-granted resolver surface — which is exactly the condition that makes the unattended
pass prompt-free. The observation stands on that mechanism.
